question: Is value-only writing capped by BANDWIDTH or by something deeper? ORACLE-WRITE measured the perfect-value write ceiling on the tf-idf top-32 slots (~9% of eval-time attention) and got MT 2.3810. DIAG-ROUTING reported mass_on_S = 0.5697 QA / 0.5879 MT at top_t=512, a claimed 6.6x bandwidth gain. Read the same write ceiling at full support.
variable_under_test: TOP_T=512 (vs TOP_T=32 in ORACLE-WRITE), for both AM_ORACLE_WRITE=1 (teacher's own document values) and AM_ORACLE_WRITE=0 (closed-form solved values); every other knob held at ORACLE-WRITE's config
baseline_ref: ORACLE-WRITE (top_t=32): oracle QA 1.8955 / MT 2.3810, control QA 2.1772 / MT 2.5524. Also DIAG-OBJ-b (top_t=512, RIDGE_LAMBDA=0): QA 2.5151 / MT 2.6652.

n_written_per_document.note: IDENTICAL for all 16 documents and all 36 layers. The MECH-001 edge case |S| > T_doc did NOT bind: every Qasper document tokenizes to >= 511 tokens, so n_written = min(|S|, T_doc) = |S| = 511 everywhere. TOP_T=512 is clamped by the ranker to k = min(top_t, n_tokens) = 511 (511 trainable + 1 frozen slot), i.e. the entire writable cartridge.
n_written_per_document.consequence: Because each document writes ALL 511 trainable slots, the 16 documents MUTUALLY OVERWRITE: the final oracle cartridge is document 16's (doc-015) mass-ranked teacher values alone, with zero Phase-1 content and zero content from documents 1-15 surviving. At top_t=32 the per-document selections overlapped only partially (union 34-82 slots/layer) so 16 documents coexisted. This is a structural property of the assigned configuration, not an artefact of the measurement.

eval_time_mass_on_S_mean_over_36_layers.definition: probability mass on S under the FULL eval-time softmax over [512 cartridge slots || own-sequence causal prefix]; S = the 511 TRAINABLE slots that were actually written (union over 16 docs = all of them).

RECONCILIATION_WITH_DIAG_ROUTING.finding: DIAG-ROUTING's 0.5697/0.5879 match our TOTAL CARTRIDGE mass to 5-6 significant figures, not the mass on the writable slots. The gap is the ONE FROZEN SLOT (index 0), which carries a mean 0.3506 (QA) / 0.3550 (MT) of total attention -- up to 0.624 in a single layer -- i.e. a classic attention sink. It is num_frozen_tokens=1 and is NEVER writable by any AM configuration.
RECONCILIATION_WITH_DIAG_ROUTING.note: The board's 6.6x figure compared the top-32 union's mass against total cartridge mass including the unwritable sink. The real writable-support gain is 2.6x, and the ceiling on any value-only write's bandwidth is ~0.23, not ~0.59.

total_cartridge_attention_mass.comparison_to_ORACLE_WRITE_top32: At top_t=32 the oracle LEFT cartridge mass at Phase-1 level (MT 0.588 -> 0.596) while the solved control COLLAPSED it (0.588 -> 0.329). At top_t=512 BOTH collapse it by a similar amount (oracle -34.3%, control -31.6%) even though the oracle's values top out at |67| and the control's at |792| -- a 12x magnitude difference. So the cartridge-mass collapse at full support tracks HOW MANY SLOTS ARE OVERWRITTEN, not the value magnitude.

per_layer_cascade_signature.interpretation: Layer 0 routing is BIT-UNCHANGED by both writes (ratio exactly 1.000), as it must be: layer-0 queries come from the token embeddings and no value write can perturb them. From layer 1 onward routing is massively rearranged -- early layers pull 2-3x MORE mass into the cartridge, layers 7+ push it out. This is a direct, per-layer measurement of the B-CASCADE mechanism (value writes perturb the residual stream, which moves later layers' queries), and layer 0 is a built-in null control proving the measurement is not an artefact.

comparison_to_DIAG_OBJ_b.note: The only config difference is RIDGE_LAMBDA (1e-4 here vs 0 there). Both deltas are inside the ~0.1-0.2 noise band, and the solve's own MSE and |v| also agree closely -- an independent replication of HYP-R0 (ridge is a wash) at full support. The solve_s difference (322 vs 184 s) is wall-clock contention with a concurrent worker on the other GPU, not a numerical difference.

diagnostics.raw_arrays: research_loop/state/diagnostics/ORACLE-WRITE-512.json (per-layer mass_on_S / mass_on_cart / share_of_cart / mass_on_S_scored arrays for all 6 cache x split combinations, per-document n_written and mean_mse, provenance block) and research_loop/state/diagnostics/ORACLE-WRITE-512_route_mass.json (the raw diagnostic dump)

observations: At full support the write-ceiling oracle does not approach the bar -- it moves sharply AWAY from it on both axes. Teacher's-own-values written into all 511 trainable slots gives QA 3.3920 / MT 3.2370 (in-run 3.3949 / 3.2404), versus the same oracle at top_t=32 (QA 1.8955 / MT 2.3810) and versus this run's own like-for-like solved control at top_t=512 (QA 2.4974 / MT 2.5757, in-run 2.4996 / 2.5771). MT is 0.856 WORSE than the top-32 oracle and 0.661 worse than the solved control at the same support; QA at 3.3920 is worse even than never writing at all (Phase-1 floor 2.2388). The control at top_t=512 reproduces DIAG-OBJ-b (top_t=511, RIDGE_LAMBDA=0: QA 2.5151 / MT 2.6652) to within the noise band on both axes (-0.016 QA, -0.088 MT), with |v| 792 vs 848 and mean_mse_last_doc 0.1601 vs 0.1687, so the only knob that differs (ridge) is again a wash. n_written is 511 for every one of the 16 documents on every one of the 36 layers -- MECH-001's |S| > T_doc edge case did NOT bind, because every Qasper document is longer than 511 tokens -- which means each document overwrites the ENTIRE writable cartridge and the 16 documents mutually overwrite, so the final oracle cache holds only document 16's values; this is a structural consequence of top_t=512 with per_layer granularity, and it is the most likely single cause of the MT regression, so the run does NOT cleanly isolate bandwidth from mutual overwrite. The standing mass_on_S requirement produced a correction to the board's premise: on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge the 511 WRITABLE slots carry 0.2190 (QA) / 0.2328 (MT) of total attention, not 0.5697 / 0.5879 -- those DIAG-ROUTING figures match our measured TOTAL cartridge mass (0.56967 / 0.58787) to 5-6 significant figures, and the 0.35 difference is the single frozen slot 0, an attention sink carrying a mean 0.3506 QA / 0.3550 MT (up to 0.624 in one layer) that no AM configuration can write; the real writable-support bandwidth gain from the tf-idf top-32 union is therefore 2.6x (0.0896 -> 0.2328 on MT), not 6.6x. After the write, mass_on_S falls further, to 0.1952 (oracle MT) and 0.1588 (control MT), and total cartridge mass collapses from 0.5879 to 0.3863 (oracle, -34.3%) and 0.4023 (control, -31.6%) -- at top_t=32 the oracle had left cartridge mass untouched (0.588 -> 0.596) while only the solved write collapsed it, so at full support the collapse happens even with teacher-scale values (|v| max 67 vs the control's 792, a 12x difference), i.e. it tracks the number of slots overwritten rather than the value magnitude. The per-layer arrays give a clean causal signature with a built-in null control: layer 0's mass on S is bit-unchanged by both writes (0.1919 -> 0.1919, ratio exactly 1.000, as required since layer-0 queries come from the embeddings), while from layer 1 onward routing is rearranged -- early layers pull 2.4-3.3x MORE mass onto the cartridge and layers 7+ push it out (min ratio 0.393 at L7 for the oracle), and the layer carrying peak mass on S moves from 28 to 2. Caveats: the eval splits are tiny (QA n=6, MT n=5 batches) so only deltas well outside ~0.1-0.2 count, and all the deltas reported here except the control-vs-DIAG-OBJ-b comparison are far outside it; the mutual-overwrite confound above means this run bounds 'value-only writing at full support as this codebase implements it' rather than 'value-only writing at 23% bandwidth' in isolation; and the oracle's assignment is mass_ranked, so a different assignment of 511 document rows to 511 slots is untested.
